operationalization: No third-person variable would be present if a tissue had experience while deciding and absent if the same tissue only carried out the same physiological dynamics.
obstacles: Phenomenal 'something it is like' has no public measurement that separates it from the physiological description of the same events.
rationale: The hypothesis is about first-person experience in non-neural organs. Neural and physiological data can describe decision-like dynamics, and those same records remain compatible with or without proto-consciousness. Nothing in current public data supplies a confirming or refuting observation.

operationalization: Re-run the deposited evolutionary pipeline for a stated objective and compare simulated behavior with the published living builds; transfer holds if built designs show the targeted behavior and shape-scrambled builds do not.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: public source code for re-evolving the in silico designs and reproducing the simulation half of the pipeline

obstacles: The paper deposits computational code only; Ethovision tracks and build videos are not in an open measurement archive.
Manual construction steps mean a simulator re-run does not test the living half of the pipeline.
rationale: The in silico design loop is specified and the code was deposited for reproduction, so that half can be re-run. The claim also requires living Xenopus builds to show the predicted behaviors, and those trajectories were published as summaries and supplementary media rather than as a downloadable track dataset. Existing materials can test the computational half and only audit the biological half.

operationalization: For the reported deciliated cardiac design, compare net displacement and heading of upright versus inverted organisms in the simulator and, where tracks exist, in the living builds; the claim holds if upright heading matches the design and inversion reduces displacement in both.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: code to re-simulate upright and inverted designs under the paper's random actuation and score net displacement

obstacles: In vivo p-values are published, but the trial-level movement tracks are not deposited.
The quantitative claim is for at least one design, so a re-run has to recover that design rather than a new evolutionary sample.
rationale: Heading and net displacement under an inversion control are standard kinematic variables, and the simulator that produced the in silico p-values is public. The living comparison rests on published statistics from one design without an open track file, so the in vivo clause cannot be remeasured. Re-simulation can confirm or refute the computational half.

operationalization: Test whether orientation-matched designs agree with the simulation more than inverted or shape-scrambled designs; design-dependence holds if the match disappears when morphology is flipped or replaced.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: simulator in which orientation and shape controls can be re-run to separate design-specific locomotion from a generic bias

obstacles: A shared physical bias could make simulation and organism agree even if the evolved shape is not the cause.
The living inversion result is a published summary for a narrow set of builds.
rationale: The interpretation is tied to a concrete control: agreement should depend on orientation if the morphology, rather than a chance match, carried the behavior. That control can be repeated in the public simulator. The living data are too narrow, and shared hydrodynamics could still favor both the model and the organism, so the causal wording is only partly separable from its rivals.

operationalization: Place particles in the simulated dish and measure cluster size or particles gathered per time for motile designs versus non-motile controls; the same contrast on living builds would test the in vivo clause.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: voxel simulator in which particle-gathering by motile designs can be re-implemented and compared with non-motile controls

obstacles: Passive sweeping by any moving object can pile particles up without a design-specific behavior.
Living aggregation is documented in figures and video, not as deposited particle tracks.
rationale: Aggregation is measurable as particle clustering, and the simulator can be extended or re-run for the in silico half. The living half is a qualitative supplementary observation. Without non-motile controls, piled debris is also what any crawler would leave behind, so the result is only partly discriminating.

operationalization: In paired trials, score collision rate, duration of mechanical contact, and number of shared revolutions, with cilia intact versus inhibited; the claim holds if orbiting bouts are more frequent when cilia are active.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: soft-body simulator used for the predicted multi-body contacts, which can be re-run for collision and orbit statistics

obstacles: Orbiting can arise from generic hydrodynamic drafting once two bodies touch.
The cilia contrast is an in vivo observation without a deposited event log.
rationale: Contact duration and revolutions are countable, and the deposited simulator covers the in silico collective runs. The cilia comparison and the living orbiting bouts are qualitative and not in that repository. Hydrodynamic sticking remains a competing account of temporary orbits, so current materials test only part of the claim.

operationalization: Re-evolve locomotion under randomly phased contractile voxels and track, across generations, shape plus the fraction of passive versus contractile cells against the variance of heading or centroid velocity; derandomization holds if coherence rises under selection and stays low in unselected controls.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: deposited evolutionary algorithm and Voxelyze engine for re-running selection on randomly actuated soft bodies

obstacles: The 2019 VoxCad build is finicky to compile, and exact seeds are needed to match historical runs.
Coherence must be defined from the supplement; several variance metrics could be computed.
rationale: The claim is about an outcome inside a specified soft-body evolutionary simulation, and the code for that simulation is public. A small team can re-evolve populations and measure whether shape and tissue arrangement reduce the randomness of global motion relative to unselected controls. That comparison confirms or refutes the derandomization result without new biological data.

operationalization: Score whether novel, nerve-free, mixed-tissue builds maintain the designed behavior and external shape; competence-as-cause would require that outcome to survive only when a separate, pre-registered measure of cell-level cooperation is intact.
obstacles: Biophysical self-assembly predicts the same maintenance of shape and movement.
No deposited dataset records a cell-level competence variable separate from the organism-level behavior.
rationale: Maintenance of designed behavior in a novel configuration is observable and is described in the published builds. Attributing that outcome to behavioral competence and cooperation, rather than to the mechanics of adhesion and contraction, has no measurement that would come apart from those mechanics. Public materials can speak to the outcome and leave the causal wording underdetermined.

operationalization: From contraction or voltage traces in built organisms, compute phase lag among cardiac regions; spontaneous coordination holds if phase-locking exceeds a shuffle of independent cells and was not imposed by the construction protocol.
obstacles: The data release covers simulation code, not cardiomyocyte timing traces.
Supplementary video, where present, is an illustration rather than a sample of phase measurements.
rationale: Phase-matched contraction is a standard physiological measurement and would be distinguishable from independent twitching. The paper reports the coordination and deposits the simulator, which assumes actuation rather than recording it. No public trace archive supports a reanalysis, so the test needs the original timing data or a new recording.

operationalization: After a standardized laceration, measure wound width over time against uninjured shape landmarks; self-repair holds if the gap closes and the external configuration returns, beyond passive recoil.
obstacles: The support is a supplementary example, not a deposited series with sample size and controls.
Tissue recoil and wound contraction can close a gap without a regulated repair response.
rationale: Wound closure and shape maintenance are measurable. The published support is an illustrative supplementary figure, and re-inspecting that figure is not a test of rates, sample size, or passive recoil. A quantitative decision needs the original time series or a new assay.

operationalization: Re-evaluate pass-1 and pass-2 designs in the deposited simulator and compute the fraction of time steps with ground contact; the numerical claim holds if pass 2 is near 93.3 percent and pass 1 near 52.7 percent under the published evaluation window.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: pass-1 and pass-2 evolutionary experiments whose ground-contact time can be recomputed in Voxelyze

obstacles: Matching the published percentages requires the same evaluation window and random seeds described in the supplement.
Living ground-contact was not deposited as a paired percentage, so the match to organisms is carried by the simulation contrast.
rationale: The quantitative content is a pair of ground-contact fractions from two specified simulation passes, and the code for those passes is public. Recomputing contact time confirms or refutes the 93.3 versus 52.7 percent contrast with a standard geometric measurement. The link to living gaits is the reason the second pass was defined, and it is checked by whether that pass stays on the substrate as the paper's living builds do.

operationalization: Shape animal-cap aggregates with concavities of graded width and record whether each gap remains after a fixed culture interval; the size threshold holds if gaps at or above 100 micrometers persist and smaller gaps close.
obstacles: The result is described as preliminary work in a supplement figure, without a deposited morphometry table.
Testing it again requires new microsurgical aggregates.
rationale: Concavity width and persistence are direct morphometric variables with a clear threshold. The published support is a preliminary supplementary figure, not an open table of widths and outcomes. Confirming or refuting the 100 micrometer cutoff requires those measurements or a new build series.

operationalization: A census of cognitive systems would need a part to count as an agent by a criterion that could fail; under the claim's usage, any functional part can be counted as an agent.
obstacles: 'Agent in important ways' can be applied to whatever parts a system has, so no catalog of organisms yields a refuting case.
rationale: Biological cognitive systems are structurally made of parts, which is true by anatomy and does not need a dataset. Calling those parts agents, and concluding there is no indivisible cognitive being, does not add an observation that would distinguish the claim from a non-agential parts list. The universal wording is fixed by the definition in use.

operationalization: Compare time-to-criterion or savings after regeneration between animals trained before decapitation and naive regenerates; persistence holds if trained animals relearn faster after a new brain is built, with motility equated.
obstacles: Raw tracking logs from the automated assay were not deposited.
Residual body tissue, sensitization, and one-tailed tests can mimic savings without a memory stored outside the original brain.
Classical manual studies and the 2013 familiarization assay do not cover the same tasks.
rationale: Memory here has a workable behavioral meaning: faster return to criterion after training, measured again after the head regenerates. Published tables from the automated familiarization study and older training papers contain summary counts, scattered across journals rather than in one archive. Those summaries can be re-read for effect direction, and they leave the main confounds and the raw latencies unchecked.

operationalization: In the light-mediated learning assay, compare choice performance of tadpoles with ectopic tail eyes and native eyes removed against blind and normal-eyed animals; visual learning holds if only animals with a functional eye-brain path exceed chance.
obstacles: Trial-level choice logs are in the papers' summaries, not a public repository.
Both positive reports come from the same group, so an independent replicate is not in the open record.
rationale: The learning assay and the blind and innervated controls map onto choice rates that the 2013 and 2017 papers publish for this Xenopus preparation. Those measurements cover the stated scope and can be checked for whether tail-eye animals outperform eyeless controls. Without deposited trial logs, a new analyst cannot recompute the statistics from raw choices.

operationalization: On one pre-registered cognitive or neural trait, test whether sister lineages differ by jumps that are large relative to within-lineage variation and short relative to individual lifespan; a continuum holds if changes are graded on that trait.
obstacles: Neuron counts, brain size, and learning scores are different operationalizations and need not agree.
A graded proxy can hide a qualitative change in a capacity the proxy does not measure.
'Have not been shown' is a claim about the literature as well as about the organisms.
rationale: Comparative compilations of brain size, neuron number, and learning scores exist as scattered published tables and can be tested for saltations versus grades on those proxies. No single public matrix covers cognition across the claim's full range of organisms, and competing proxies answer differently. The result can pressure a strong binary reading and cannot settle cognitive capacity as such.

operationalization: Model comparison can rank which description predicts and controls a system most efficiently, and under this claim the winner is the correct agency level by definition.
obstacles: Every outcome of a predictive comparison is compatible with the claim, because the claim stipulates that the best-controlling model is the right level of agency.
rationale: The statement is a rule for attributing agency: use whichever model gives the most efficient prediction and control. Experiments can rank models, and the ranking cannot come out against the rule, because the rule defines the preferred level as the winner. That is a methodological stipulation rather than a result public data could refute.

operationalization: On published GRN models, pair a cue with an outcome-producing stimulus and test whether the cue later changes the response relative to unpaired controls; associative learning, pattern completion, or generalization holds if the paired network meets that criterion and a shuffled network does not.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Collective
candidate_datasets.role: public Boolean gene-regulatory models, including the networks used in the cited memory surveys

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public ODE models of biological pathways that can be re-simulated for stimulus-pairing tests

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: code for a follow-up memory screen of continuous BioModels networks

obstacles: Code for the 2021 Boolean memory screen was withheld, so the exact published runs cannot be replayed.
Associative learning, pattern completion, and generalization are defined differently across the cited papers.
rationale: The models themselves are public, in Cell Collective and BioModels, and a later ODE analysis has open code, so a defined pairing protocol can be re-run. The flagship Boolean analysis did not release its code, and the cited papers do not share one decision rule. A new screen can test learning capacity in the published models and will not automatically reproduce each cited result.

operationalization: Goals, associative memory, and credit assignment can be measured in a particular system, but finding them would illustrate this definition of a Self rather than test it.
obstacles: The statement stipulates the hallmarks of a Self, so empirical cases are examples of the definition.
rationale: The text presents these three capacities as the basic hallmarks TAME will use. A system that shows them fits the definition, and a system that lacks them falls outside it. Public data can hunt for the capacities and cannot confirm or refute the stipulation that they are what a Self is.

operationalization: The spatial and temporal reach of a measured setpoint can be plotted, and the claim then calls that plot the boundary of the Self.
obstacles: Once goal scale is measured, identifying it with the boundary of the Self is true by the proposed diagram, with no rival outcome.
rationale: Spatiotemporal scale of a homeostatic target is something an experiment could estimate for a given system. The claim uses that scale as the delineation of the Self, which is the framework's classification rule. Any measured scale is compatible with the rule, so the statement does not have a separate empirical consequence.

operationalization: Impose a local deviation from a measured setpoint, record whether distant modules change their activity, and block the candidate signal; binding holds if remote action reduces the original error and fails when the signal is blocked.
obstacles: Ordinary physiological coupling spreads signals without binding modules into one homeostatic individual.
Setpoint error, remote recruitment, and error reduction are rarely measured together outside a few injury preparations.
Published injury-spread results cover a small slice of multicellular organisms.
rationale: Long-range injury signals and compensatory responses are reported in a handful of regeneration papers, as summaries rather than a shared dataset. Those records can show that a wound changes distant tissue. They do not contain the joint measurement of setpoint error, recruitment, and error reduction that would separate one homeostatic loop from ordinary coupling.

operationalization: Date gene families used in physiological and morphogenetic control against the origin of nervous systems and 3D behavioral circuits; the sequential claim is supported only as a proxy if those families are older and later co-opted into neural control.

candidate_datasets.name: OrthoDB
candidate_datasets.role: phyletic profiles of gene families to see which physiological and morphogenetic regulators predate nervous systems

candidate_datasets.name: Ensembl
candidate_datasets.role: annotated metazoan genomes for presence of the same families in aneural and neural lineages

candidate_datasets.name: TimeTree
candidate_datasets.role: clade divergence times for ordering those gene origins against the origin of nervous systems

obstacles: Shared genes are compatible with later co-option and do not show that behavioral strategies are variants of older ones.
Problem-solving in metabolic or morphogenetic space is not a variable in these databases.
rationale: Public orthology and divergence-time resources can test whether components of physiological and morphogenetic control are older than nervous systems. That is a proxy for the proposed timeline. The claim that 3D behavioral problem-solving is the same strategy pivoted into a new space is not distinguished by gene age alone.

operationalization: Reanalyze GSE98084 for the fraction of transcripts that change in barium-adapted heads versus wild-type heads, and compare that count with the paper's survival and regeneration tallies in BaCl2; the transcriptional clause holds if only a small fraction of the transcriptome moves.

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: series GSE98084, public RNA-seq of barium-adapted versus wild-type Dugesia japonica heads, for recounting differentially expressed transcripts

obstacles: Two biological replicates limit how firmly 'relatively few genes' can be reestimated.
Head loss and later barium insensitivity are phenotype counts in the paper, not in the expression series.
Differential expression does not show that the cells searched transcriptional space for a solution evolution had not already produced.
rationale: The expression half is in a public RNA-seq series and can be reanalyzed with a standard differential-expression pipeline. Phenotype claims, that heads are lost and the regenerated heads are barium-insensitive, sit in the paper's counts with no separate deposited assay table. The navigational reading of those gene changes is not separated by the expression matrix from a narrower physiological compensation.

operationalization: Track craniofacial organ positions from scrambled tadpole arrangements through metamorphosis and test whether endpoints cluster on the normal frog-face coordinates even when the paths are abnormal or overshoot.
obstacles: Landmark time series are published as paper figures and summaries, not as a deposited coordinate table.
Mechanical packing in the head could funnel organs toward the same endpoints.
rationale: Endpoint position versus path shape is a direct test, and the Xenopus craniofacial papers report morphometrics for this preparation, including abnormal paths and overshoot. Those measurements are scattered in journal figures rather than an open coordinate file. They can support the setpoint reading for this species and leave mechanical funneling as a live alternative.

operationalization: Pair the location of an antler wound in one year with tine positions after shedding, against unwounded antlers; a rewritable target holds if ectopic tines recur at the wound site and can be changed by a later injury.
obstacles: The observations are case reports and older natural-history figures, not a coordinate database.
Local scar, pedicle damage, or broken bone can place a tine without a rewritten morphological setpoint.
Few species and few animals are described quantitatively.
rationale: Location-specific ectopic tines in later antler cycles are described in published case literature and could be compiled for a weak spatial test. There is no public table of wound coordinates, subsequent tines, and controls. Scar and structural damage remain competing accounts, so existing reports can illustrate the pattern and cannot settle the memory interpretation.

operationalization: Count heads, and compare head and brain landmarks to reference species, after gap-junction or ion-channel perturbation versus vehicle; the claim holds if one, two, and zero heads, and non-native head shapes, occur above the vehicle rate.

candidate_datasets.name: Planform
candidate_datasets.role: curated database of published planarian regeneration experiments, including drug treatments and organ-level morphologies

obstacles: Most quantitative series come from one laboratory, and raw images are not in a measurement archive.
Planform encodes published outcomes and may omit landmark-level shapes from later papers.
Toxicity can change head number unless vehicle and washout controls are carried along.
rationale: Head number and morphometric distance to reference species are standard variables, and several papers publish counts for gap-junction and channel perturbations in regenerating planaria. Planform compiles literature experiments of this kind, while the underlying images and landmarks remain in the papers. The phenotypic claim can be audited for the reported species and manipulations, short of an independent raw-data reanalysis.

operationalization: Cut transiently treated two-headed or zero-headed worms with no further drug and score head number in successive regenerates, alongside a wild-type sequence or drug-residue assay; persistence holds if abnormal head number continues after the drug is gone and the genome matches wild type.

candidate_datasets.name: Planform
candidate_datasets.role: encoded published regeneration outcomes, including head number after pharmacological treatments, for experiments that were curated

obstacles: Penetrance tables are in the papers, not as animal-level files.
Residual drug or a selected genetic variant can mimic a permanent physiological state.
Wild-type genome is argued from induction and reset experiments more often than from deposited sequence of the altered lines.
rationale: Head counts across amputation rounds with no further treatment are published for the octanol and related protocols. Planform may contain the curated head-number outcomes; it does not replace the raw counts. Persistence can be checked at the level of those published penetrances, and the genetic-wild-type clause stays weakly tested without sequence of the same lines.

operationalization: Apply a transient bioelectric perturbation, remove it, and test whether a new regenerative target persists across further amputations; the memory reading holds if the new target remains after tissue composition and channel expression have returned to the original state.

candidate_datasets.name: Planform
candidate_datasets.role: published planarian drug and regeneration records that capture stable changes in head number after treatment

obstacles: A lasting change in cell composition or channel expression is a non-memory account of the same regenerative outcome.
Data are concentrated in planaria, while the claim says the mechanism is conserved across regenerating animals.
The optogenetic analogy is not a separate measurement.
rationale: A regenerative target that outlasts a transient gap-junction or channel treatment is documented for planaria in published penetrance data and, where curated, in Planform. Calling that change a false pattern memory, and a conserved mechanism across animals, goes beyond those head-number records. Tissue state and expression can carry the same persistence, and other taxa are thinly covered.

operationalization: In polyploid newt larvae, count cells per tubule cross-section, cell size, and lumen diameter; the anatomical claim holds if larger cells yield fewer cells per cross-section and the largest cells form a one-cell lumen of normal size.
obstacles: The measurements are in 1945 plates and counts, not a digital archive.
Cytoskeletal bending versus cell-cell signaling was inferred from the geometry, not measured with molecular markers.
The sample is one amphibian under classical polyploidy methods.
rationale: Cell number, cell size, and lumen size are the variables Fankhauser published for newt tubules, including the single-cell case. Those counts can be compiled from the papers and cannot be remeasured from a public image set. The further claim that distinct molecular mechanisms are deployed for the same lumen is an interpretation of the geometry rather than a result in the old plates.

operationalization: Decode amputation level and injury type from images of the uninjured contralateral limb at 30 seconds, against sham and dye-only controls; readout holds if classification accuracy exceeds chance at that latency.
obstacles: The published assay soaks tissue in voltage dye for about 30 minutes and reports depolarization by about one hour, so the 30-second clause is not in those summaries.
Images and animal-level measurements were not deposited.
DiBAC fluorescence is not a pure membrane-voltage measurement, and the mirror-neuron wording is not a variable in the assay.
rationale: The 2018 Xenopus study publishes correlations between stump geometry and the spatial extent of contralateral dye signal, which can be checked as a somatotopic association. The imaging window in that paper is dye incubation and a response on the order of an hour, and the images are not in a repository. The 30-second latency and the mirror-neuron description cannot be resolved from the published summaries.

operationalization: Test enrichment between morphogenesis genes and learning or memory genes after removing ion channels, connexins, and neurotransmitter machinery, using a degree-matched null; also test whether learning and memory genes are enriched in cancer, regeneration, and embryogenesis gene sets.

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Ontology
candidate_datasets.role: public gene annotations for morphogenesis, learning, memory, regeneration, and embryonic development, with evidence codes for an overlap test

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public genetic-association results for asking whether learning and memory genes recur in studies of other traits, including disease

obstacles: GO annotations are biased toward human, mouse, and heavily studied genes.
Regeneration genetics is largely RNAi and mutant screens, which are less completely captured by GO and the GWAS Catalog than cancer is.
rationale: Both clauses are gene-set comparisons, and the annotations and association catalogs needed for them are public and standard to analyze in days. Removing the already-shared channel, connexin, and transmitter genes is a pre-registered way to test specificity, and a null result would refute excess overlap. Coverage is weaker for regeneration screens and for non-mammalian animals than for human learning and development genes, which limits scope rather than blocking the test.

operationalization: Deliver a nutrient, endorphin, or shock contingency contingent on an anatomical or expression state, against a yoked non-contingent control; trainability holds if only the contingent group moves toward the rewarded morphology.
obstacles: No public experiment pairs contingent reward or punishment with a morphological endpoint.
Later discussions and proposed reinforcement protocols have not released such an outcome dataset.
rationale: A reinforcement test with yoked controls would cleanly confirm or refute trainability of a morphological outcome. The source paper marks the experiment as not yet done, and public follow-up through 2026 is proposal and framework rather than a deposited training result. The necessary measurements are still to be collected.

operationalization: Simulate a transient voltage pulse with published channel and connexin gating and test for two stable voltages or coupling states; dynamical memory holds if the post-pulse state remains after the pulse and changes later input-output behavior with the same hardware.

candidate_datasets.name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology
candidate_datasets.role: curated gating and ligand data for voltage-gated channels and connexins used to parameterize a memory simulation

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: published differential-equation models of excitable membranes and gap-junction coupling that can be re-integrated

obstacles: Most kinetic parameters come from neurons or heterologous cells, not the non-neural tissues in the claim.
A persistent voltage in real tissue can be transcriptional or ultrastructural rather than a dynamical-system memory of the same channels.
rationale: Voltage-gated channel and connexin kinetics are public, and published ODE models can be re-run to see whether a transient voltage leaves a stable state. That tests the biophysical implication in models. It does not cover non-neural tissues generally, and tissue experiments that would separate dynamical memory from a changed proteome are not in one open dataset.

operationalization: Tracer studies can show that material crossing a gap junction carries no origin label, and the same records are what a larger Self and ordinary shared cytoplasm both predict.
obstacles: Loss of a diffusion barrier and formation of a larger Self predict the same coupling, coordination, and shared signals.
rationale: Gap junctions pass small molecules without tagging the sender, which follows from the structure of the pore and is already standard physiology. The further claim that this erasure creates a larger Self working toward common goals uses those same coupling facts. No additional observation would favor the Self wording over shared signals through open junctions.

operationalization: Compare connexin expression, and where available dye-coupling, between transformed and matched normal tissue, and between carcinogen-exposed and control cells; the physiological clause holds if coupling falls as transformation proceeds.

candidate_datasets.name: Genomic Data Commons
candidate_datasets.role: TCGA and related tumor expression for connexin genes across cancers, a proxy for gap-junction status

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: public expression series after carcinogen exposure or oncogene activation that include gap-junction transcripts

obstacles: Transcript abundance is not gap-junction closure or dye coupling.
Connexin loss is common in tumors and is neither necessary nor sufficient for transformation.
A shrinking computational Self is not a separate variable from loss of coupling and altered growth.
rationale: Public tumor and exposure expression archives can test whether connexin genes fall with transformation, which is the measurable core of the gap-junction clause. Functional closure is only in scattered dye-transfer papers. The reading that cancer is a reversion to unicellular selves with smaller computational boundaries is not distinguished by those expression patterns from loss of coupling plus proliferation.

operationalization: Score melanocyte conversion in wild-type Xenopus after a bioelectric perturbation, and score tumor-like structures in p53 or KRAS backgrounds with and without a normalizing voltage manipulation; override holds if incidence moves in the predicted direction on a wild-type genome.
obstacles: Counts are in the Xenopus papers, not a deposited animal-level table.
The readouts are embryo pigment and tumor-like foci, a narrow stand-in for metastatic melanoma and clinical reversion.
The positive series are from one laboratory.
rationale: Incidence of the reported Xenopus phenotypes under voltage manipulation, with and without oncogenes, is published with controls and covers the claim's stated embryo scope. Those numbers can be audited and cannot be recomputed from raw images, because no image or count archive was released. The jump from these foci to metastatic melanoma in general is outside what the measurements contain.

operationalization: Map ion-channel, connexin, and innexin families onto aneural animals and their unicellular relatives versus the origin of neurons; precedence of the genes holds if the families are present before nervous systems, which still leaves their developmental use untested.

candidate_datasets.name: OrthoDB
candidate_datasets.role: ortholog presence of bioelectric gene families in sponges, placozoans, ctenophores, and choanoflagellates

candidate_datasets.name: Ensembl
candidate_datasets.role: annotated genomes for the same early-branching animals and for animals with nervous systems

obstacles: Gene presence in a sponge or placozoan does not show that the genes were used to place the body in morphospace.
Channels have many functions besides positional control, so their age is compatible with other histories.
rationale: Public genomes can show that many bioelectric gene families occur in animals without neurons and in close unicellular relatives, which bears on which hardware came first. The claim also says evolution used analog bioelectric dynamics to position body configuration before neural spiking. That use is not a column in the genome matrices, so gene age is only a partial test.

operationalization: Build a presence-absence matrix of voltage- and ligand-gated channel families across unicellular eukaryotes and early metazoans and test whether context-sensitive families originate at the metazoan node, alongside gains in body-plan complexity.

candidate_datasets.name: OrthoDB
candidate_datasets.role: phyletic profiles for ion-channel families across unicellular eukaryotes and early animals

candidate_datasets.name: UniProt
candidate_datasets.role: protein sequences and functional notes for classifying channels as voltage- or ligand-gated

candidate_datasets.name: InterPro
candidate_datasets.role: domain annotations used to detect channel families in genomes that lack detailed physiology

obstacles: Domain presence is an imperfect stand-in for context-sensitive gating.
Channel gains at the origin of animals coincide with many other novelties, so a correlation does not isolate body-plan complexity.
The further continuum from excitability through somatic patterning to cognition is not in these matrices.
rationale: Channel-family presence across choanoflagellates, sponges, ctenophores, and cnidarians can be rebuilt from public orthology and domain databases with a standard phylogenetic presence-absence analysis. That tests whether context-sensitive families appear with metazoan complexity, within the limits of domain-based classification. It does not test the claimed continuum onward to cognition.

operationalization: Score eye markers and lens or retinal histology in gut, spinal cord, and posterior tissue after misexpression of one ion channel, and run Pax6 at the same sites; the contrast holds if the channel induces complete eyes where Pax6 does not.
obstacles: Histology and induction rates are in the papers, not a public image archive.
The Pax6 comparison comes from a separate vertebrate study, so sites and criteria are not matched in one dataset.
'Complete eye' has been scored with markers and anatomy of varying stringency.
rationale: Induction frequency and histological completeness are measurable, and the channel and Pax6 papers publish those observations for ectopic sites. They are not deposited as reanalyzable images, and the Pax6 insufficiency claim rests on a different experimental series. Existing write-ups can partially audit the contrast and cannot re-score the sections.

operationalization: Test whether mutations in electrogenic genes produce coordinated, multi-site anatomical changes, using zebrafish genotype-phenotype records, and separately test whether KCNH8 or a connexin is causal in the fish fin shift rather than merely differentially expressed.

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: zebrafish genotype-phenotype records for electrogenic mutants, including fin morphologies, as a partial test that such mutations can reshape anatomy

obstacles: The cited fish-fin result identifies KCNH8 and a connexin in a transcriptome of a developing ornament, which is expression rather than a demonstrated causal mutation.
A raw RNA-seq accession for that study was not confirmed here, so the expression list cannot be assumed reanalyzable from a named archive.
Zebrafish fin mutants do not establish the evolutionary swap of channels in the swordtail case.
rationale: Zebrafish phenotype databases record anatomical effects of mutations in some potassium-channel genes, which can test the narrower claim that electrogenic mutations can change morphology in a coordinated way. The evolutionary example is a candidate-gene expression result during fin outgrowth, and differential expression does not show that a mutation caused the species difference. Public data therefore cover a related genetic possibility and leave the historical case weakly tested.

operationalization: In an evolutionary simulation, compare the fitness effect and fixation of a morphology-displacing mutation with and without a module that corrects anatomy toward a target; shielding holds if the same mutation is more nearly neutral when correction is present.
obstacles: No deposited simulation was found that already compares fitness landscapes with and without morphogenetic correction.
Comparative mutational-robustness data for regulative versus mosaic developers are too sparse to stand in for that contrast.
rationale: The prediction has a clear computational contrast: the same disruptive mutation should be less visible to selection when competent modules correct anatomy. That run was not located as public code or output, and organismal datasets do not contain the paired with-versus-without comparison. Resolving the claim needs that simulation or a new comparative measurement.

operationalization: Repair of injury and correction of a mutational displacement use the same homeostasis measurements, so either selective history remains compatible with the same present-day data.
obstacles: A mechanism that corrects both wounds and mutational deviations does not record which of those roles was the primary historical reason.
rationale: Anatomical homeostasis can be shown to reduce error after cuts and after experimental displacements, and both results fit a system shaped by injury, by mutation, or by both. The claim is about the primary evolutionary reason. Present physiological and phylogenetic records do not separate that historical purpose from the other.

operationalization: No public measurement would be positive if a morphogenetic or transcriptional system had a minimal degree of consciousness and negative if it only regulated those variables.
obstacles: Degree of consciousness, as first-person experience, is not separated by any dataset from competent regulation in the same state space.
rationale: The statement infers a minimal degree of consciousness for systems whose perception and action are in morphogenetic or transcriptional spaces. Regulation, goal-like setpoints, and transcriptional change are measurable, and those measurements are exactly what a non-conscious account of the same systems also predicts. No existing dataset draws the distinction.

operationalization: Compare anesthetic potency at connexins with potency at primary targets such as GABA-A receptors, and test whether selective gap-junction blockers stop organism-level behavior in plants, Hydra, and animals while cell viability remains.

candidate_datasets.name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology
candidate_datasets.role: curated target and ligand records for anesthetics, connexins, and the primary neural receptors

candidate_datasets.name: ChEMBL
candidate_datasets.role: public bioactivity values for asking whether general anesthetics block gap junctions at concentrations that anesthetize

obstacles: Many anesthetics act on synaptic receptors at concentrations below those reported for connexin block.
Behavioral arrest in plants and Hydra is in a few papers, not in these pharmacology databases.
Disappearance of a higher-level Self is not a variable separate from loss of coordinated behavior.
rationale: Pharmacology databases can test whether general anesthetics inhibit connexins, and at what concentration relative to their main targets. That addresses the gap-junction-blocker clause and can fail it for agents whose clinical action is elsewhere. Loss of a higher-level Self, and anesthesia by gap-junction block from plants to humans, is only partly represented by those ligand tables.

operationalization: After a brief octanol exposure, classify regenerated Girardia head shape against reference species at the end of regeneration and again weeks later; the morphological claim holds if non-native shapes are enriched early and then return to the species-typical shape.

candidate_datasets.name: Planform
candidate_datasets.role: curated planarian regeneration morphologies, useful for drug-induced head outcomes that were encoded from the literature

obstacles: Landmark coordinates and time courses live in the 2015 paper and its supplement, not as a confirmed open morphometric file.
Planform may store categorical outcomes rather than the remodeling trajectory.
The parallel with anesthesia is an interpretation and is not tested by head shape.
rationale: Species-likeness scores over time are a direct test, and the octanol study publishes morphometrics and a later return to Girardia shape for this protocol. Planform can hold curated morphology outcomes and does not replace those landmarks. The shape time course can be audited from the paper, and the analogy to loss and return of a Self under anesthesia is not an additional empirical result in the data.
